```{r shared-setup}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
source("scripts/analysis_setup.R")

# Sort key for bar charts: by share, with any "Other..." category last
# (Wilke ch. 6: order by value; a catch-all category is not part of that order).
other_last <- function(label, value) {
  label <- as.character(label)
  case_when(
    startsWith(label, "Other") | label == "Countries at <2%" ~ -Inf,
    label == "1 respondent" ~ -2,
    label == "2 respondents" ~ -1,
    TRUE ~ value
  )
}

# Bar value labels (audit V17h): whole percent from 2% up; below 2% one decimal,
# so that e.g. one and two respondents (0.7% and 1.3%) do not both read "1%".
percent_label <- function(x) {
  if_else(round(x, 1) < 2, sprintf("%.1f%%", x), paste0(round(x), "%"))
}

format_category_labels <- function(labels) {
  lapply(
    labels,
    \(label) {
      if (identical(label, "Other")) {
        bquote(italic(.(label)))
      } else {
        label
      }
    }
  )
}
```

## Included sample: N = `r nrow(data)`

The analysis includes `r nrow(data)` respondents after applying the study's date and completion criteria.

```{r sample-summary}
tibble(
  respondents = nrow(data),
  mean_completion_minutes = mean(as.numeric(data$TIME_SUM), na.rm = TRUE) / 60,
  median_completion_minutes = median(as.numeric(data$TIME_SUM), na.rm = TRUE) / 60
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = c(0, 1, 1),
    col.names = c(
      "Respondents",
      "Mean completion time (minutes)",
      "Median completion time (minutes)"
    ),
    caption = "Summary of the included sample.",
    align = c("r", "r", "r"),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

## Sample definition

```{r data-quality}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
source(project_path("scripts", "data_quality.R"))
# "24 Jul 2026"; month.abb is English regardless of the system locale
format_day_month_year <- function(d) {
  sprintf("%d %s %s", as.integer(format(d, "%d")),
          month.abb[as.integer(format(d, "%m"))], format(d, "%Y"))
}
```

- **Launch date.** Records started before `r format_day_month_year(study_launch_date)` are
  excluded. They are test runs of the questionnaire: `r n_pre_launch_completed` completed
  records, all from `r paste(format_day_month_year(pre_launch_dates), collapse = ", ")`.
- **Completion.** Only records that reached page 51 are analysed. Page 51 (open
  feedback) is the last questionnaire page; pages 52–53 only lead to the optional raffle.
  Records that stopped there, or that SoSci Survey does not flag as finished, therefore
  contain the whole questionnaire. `r n_incomplete_after_launch` records started after
  launch did not reach page 51.
- **Quality control.** `r length(flagged_ids)` participants are flagged for possibly
  careless answering but kept in all main analyses; see the
  [Quality control](quality.qmd) page.

## Self-assessed visualization experience

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.5
n_total <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(A001)) %>%
  nrow()

data$A001 %>% table() %>%  data.frame() %>% dplyr::rename(level = !!names(.)[1]) %>%
    mutate(percent_score = round(Freq / sum(Freq) * 100)) %>% 
    # Expert on top, as in the multipanel participant figures (audit V17g).
    mutate(level = factor(level, levels = c("Beginner", "Intermediate", "Expert"))) %>% 
    ggplot(data = ., aes(y = level, x = percent_score)) +  
    geom_col(stat="identity",  width = 0.8, fill ="#6BAED6") + labs(x = "Percent of respondents", y = "", title="Self-assessed level") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(percent_score, "%")), hjust = -0.2)  +  plot_theme(base_size = 20) + 
 scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Percent of respondents",
    labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    breaks = seq(0, 50, 10),

    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      transform = ~ . * n_total / 100,
      name = "Number of respondents"
    ),

    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = format_category_labels) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 22,
      face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = 14)
    ),
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 20, hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(t = 10),
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )  + coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
```

## Country of work

::: {.callout-note title="Respondents by country of work (table)" collapse="true"}
```{r}
# Answers that are not a country: the explicit refusal, and occupations entered
# in the free-text field. Both are excluded from the country percentages.
country_refusal_entries <- c("Prefer not to say")
country_occupation_entries <- c("Professor", "Senior Researcher")

country_all <- data %>%
  transmute(
    country_raw = trimws(case_when(
      A004 == "-2" & !is.na(A004s) & A004s != "" ~ A004s,
      TRUE ~ A004
    ))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    country_work = case_when(
      country_raw %in% c("NL", "Nl", "The Netherlands") ~ "Netherlands",
      country_raw == "fr" ~ "France",
      country_raw == "UK" ~ "United Kingdom",
      country_raw %in% c("United States", "United States of America") ~ "USA",
      country_raw %in% c(country_refusal_entries, country_occupation_entries) ~
        NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ country_raw
    )
  )
country_responses <- country_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(country_work), country_work != "")
country_n_refused <- sum(country_all$country_raw %in% country_refusal_entries)
country_n_occupation <- sum(country_all$country_raw %in% country_occupation_entries)
country_n_missing <- nrow(country_all) - nrow(country_responses) -
  country_n_refused - country_n_occupation

make_geography_plot <- function(summary_data, category, title,
                                respondent_total = sum(summary_data$Freq),
                                percent_formatter = percent_label) {
  category <- rlang::enquo(category)
  summary_data <- summary_data %>%
    mutate(.percent_label = percent_formatter(percent_score))

  summary_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(percent_score, fct_reorder(!!category, other_last(!!category, percent_score)))) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, fill = "#6BAED6") +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = .percent_label),
      hjust = -0.15,
      size = 6
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      "Percent of respondents",
      labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        ~ . * respondent_total / 100,
        name = "Number of respondents"
      ),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = format_category_labels) +
    labs(title = title, y = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    plot_theme(base_size = 20) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 22),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
    )
}

country <- country_responses %>%
  mutate(
    country_work = fct_lump_min(
      factor(country_work),
      min = 2,
      other_level = "Other"
    )
  ) %>% count(country_work, name = "Freq") %>%
  mutate(
    percent_score = Freq / sum(Freq) * 100,
    country_work = fct_reorder(
      country_work,
      percent_score
    ),
    country_work = fct_recode(country_work, UK = "United Kingdom")
  )
country |>
  arrange(desc(Freq)) |>
  mutate(
    country_work = as.character(country_work),
    country_work = if_else(
      country_work == "Other",
      "<em>Other</em>",
      country_work
    ),
    percent_score = paste0(round(percent_score), "%")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Country of work",
      "Respondents",
      "Percent of respondents"
    ),
    caption = "Respondents by country of work.",
    align = c("l", "r", "r"),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

### Below 2% grouped

```{r}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.8
# Country name followed by its flag (flags line up in a column at the axis).
# Flags: figures/flags/<iso2>.png from flagcdn.com, see figures/flags/SOURCES.md.
flag_tag <- function(iso, height = 11, width = 18) {
  flag_width <- if_else(!is.na(iso) & iso == "ch", height, width)
  sprintf(
    "<img src='%s' width='%d' height='%d'/>",
    project_path("figures", "flags", paste0(iso, ".png")),
    flag_width,
    height
  )
}

flag_label <- function(labels, height = 11, width = 18) {
  labels <- as.character(labels)
  display_labels <- if_else(labels == "United Kingdom", "UK", labels)
  other <- startsWith(labels, "Other")
  iso <- rep(NA_character_, length(labels))
  iso[!other] <- tolower(countrycode::countrycode(
    labels[!other], "country.name", "iso2c",
    custom_match = c(USA = "US", UK = "GB"), warn = FALSE
  ))
  dplyr::case_when(
    labels == "Other" ~ "*Other*",
    labels == "Countries at <2%" ~ "Countries at &lt;2%",
    other ~ sub("^Other \\((.*)\\)$", "*Other*<br>(\\1)", gsub("<", "&lt;", labels)),
    is.na(iso) ~ display_labels,
    TRUE ~ sprintf("%s %s", display_labels, flag_tag(iso, height, width))
  )
}

# Pool countries with less than 2% of respondents into one bar.
country_grouped <- country %>%
  mutate(country_work = as.character(country_work)) %>%
  mutate(country_work = if_else(
    percent_score < 2 | country_work == "Other", "Countries at <2%", country_work
  )) %>%
  group_by(country_work) %>%
  summarise(Freq = sum(Freq), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(percent_score = Freq / sum(Freq) * 100)

make_geography_plot(country_grouped, country_work, NULL) +
  x_axis_end_mark() +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = flag_label) +
  theme(axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 20, lineheight = 0.7))
```

### All countries

```{r}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.7
# The section heading is the title (Wilke ch. 22), so no in-figure title.
# Countries whose individual percentage would round to 1% are split into rows
# for one and two respondents. Each bar shows its row's combined share.
country_counts_all <- country_responses %>%
  count(country_work) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_score = n / nrow(country_responses) * 100,
    displayed_percent = round(percent_score)
  )
small_countries <- country_counts_all %>%
  filter(displayed_percent == 1) %>%
  arrange(country_work) %>%
  group_by(n) %>%
  mutate(
    group_percent = sum(percent_score),
    flag_index = row_number()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(iso = tolower(countrycode::countrycode(
    country_work, "country.name", "iso2c", warn = FALSE
  )))
# One flag per text box at even spacing (gridtext ignores spaces between images).
small_country_flags <- small_countries %>%
  transmute(
    x = group_percent + 3.5 + 1.2 * (flag_index - 1),
    y = if_else(
      n == 1,
      "1 respondent",
      "2 respondents"
    ),
    label = flag_tag(iso)
  )
country_all <- country_counts_all %>%
  mutate(country_work = case_when(
    displayed_percent == 1 & n == 1 ~ "1 respondent",
    displayed_percent == 1 ~ "2 respondents",
    TRUE ~ country_work
  )) %>%
  group_by(country_work) %>%
  summarise(
    Freq = sum(n),
    percent_score = sum(percent_score),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

small_group_percentages <- small_countries %>%
  distinct(group_percent) %>%
  pull(group_percent)

make_geography_plot(country_all, country_work, NULL,
                    respondent_total = nrow(country_responses),
                    percent_formatter = \(x) if_else(
                      x %in% small_group_percentages,
                      sprintf("%.1f%%", x),
                      percent_label(x)
                    )) +
  x_axis_end_mark() +
  ggtext::geom_richtext(
    data = small_country_flags,
    aes(x, y, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, label.colour = NA,
    label.padding = grid::unit(0, "pt")
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = flag_label) +
  theme(axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 20, lineheight = 0.7))
```

#### Shaded countries

```{r country-count-map}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-alt: "World map of participant counts by country of work in Equal Earth projection, with a binned legend. Darker blue indicates more participants; light grey indicates none."

country_counts <- country_responses |>
  mutate(
    map_region = case_when(
      country_work == "United Kingdom" ~ "UK",
      country_work == "Czechia" ~ "Czech Republic",
      country_work == "T\u00fcrkiye" ~ "Turkey",
      TRUE ~ country_work
    )
  ) |>
  count(map_region, name = "participants")

# Clip polygons at the antimeridian so that no country (e.g., Russia, Fiji)
# is drawn as a band stretched across the whole map after projection.
world_map <- ggplot2::map_data("world", wrap = c(-180, 180)) |>
  filter(region != "Antarctica")

unmapped_countries <- country_counts |>
  anti_join(distinct(world_map, region), by = c("map_region" = "region"))
if (nrow(unmapped_countries) > 0) {
  stop("Countries missing from the map: ",
       paste(unmapped_countries$map_region, collapse = ", "))
}

# Equal Earth projection (Šavrič, Patterson & Jenny, 2018): an equal-area
# pseudocylindrical projection, so country areas are not inflated toward the
# poles as in Mercator.
project_equal_earth <- function(lon, lat) {
  a1 <- 1.340264
  a2 <- -0.081106
  a3 <- 0.000893
  a4 <- 0.003796
  lambda <- lon * pi / 180
  theta <- asin(sqrt(3) / 2 * sin(lat * pi / 180))
  tibble::tibble(
    x = 2 * sqrt(3) * lambda * cos(theta) /
      (3 * (9 * a4 * theta^8 + 7 * a3 * theta^6 + 3 * a2 * theta^2 + a1)),
    y = a4 * theta^9 + a3 * theta^7 + a2 * theta^3 + a1 * theta
  )
}

# Binned sequential scale: grey for no participants, then light-to-dark blue.
count_breaks <- c(0, 1, 3, 6, 12, Inf)
count_labels <- c("0", "1", "2–3", "4–6", "7–12", "13+")
count_colors <- c(
  "#E3E3E3", "#C6DBEF", "#9ECAE1", "#6BAED6", "#3182BD", "#08519C"
)
names(count_colors) <- count_labels

world_map <- world_map |>
  left_join(country_counts, by = c("region" = "map_region")) |>
  mutate(
    participants = coalesce(participants, 0L),
    count_bin = cut(
      participants,
      breaks = c(-Inf, count_breaks),
      labels = count_labels,
      right = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  bind_cols(project_equal_earth(world_map$long, world_map$lat))

country_count_map <- ggplot(world_map, aes(x, y, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(
    aes(fill = count_bin),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    "Participants",
    values = count_colors,
    breaks = count_labels,
    drop = FALSE,
    guide = guide_legend(
      nrow = 1,
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      label.position = "bottom",
      keywidth = grid::unit(3.2, "lines"),
      keyheight = grid::unit(0.9, "lines")
    )
  ) +
  coord_fixed(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Participants by country of work",
    caption = paste0(
      "N = ", sum(country_counts$participants),
      " respondents with a country of work; ",
      n_distinct(country_counts$map_region), " countries.",
      " Equal Earth projection."
    )
  ) +
  theme_void(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 15) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 11, colour = "grey30"),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.key.spacing.x = grid::unit(0, "pt"),
    legend.key = element_rect(colour = NA)
  )

country_count_map

ggsave_st(
  project_path("figures", "country_work_participant_map.png"),
  country_count_map,
  width = 12,
  height = 6.2,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 180,
  device = ragg::agg_png,
  bg = "white"
)
```

#### Proportional symbols

```{r country-symbol-map-geometry}
#| include: false
# Layout of the proportional-symbol map, computed from the map geometry so that
# neither map panel is padded with white space.
# World extent: from land polygons above a small area threshold, so specks near
# the antimeridian (Fiji, Samoa, Tonga, ...) do not stretch the bounding box.
symbol_world_extent <- world_map |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(
    polygon_area = abs(sum(x * c(y[-1], y[1]) - c(x[-1], x[1]) * y)) / 2
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(polygon_area >= 5e-4)
symbol_world_xlim <- range(symbol_world_extent$x)
symbol_world_ylim <- range(symbol_world_extent$y)

# Europe inset: a lon/lat box projected like the map.
europe_box <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  lon = seq(-12, 35, length.out = 40),
  lat = seq(35, 63, length.out = 40)
) |>
  (\(box) project_equal_earth(box$lon, box$lat))()
europe_xlim <- range(europe_box$x)
europe_ylim <- range(europe_box$y)

# Column widths and row heights that match both aspect ratios: world map on the
# left over the full height; Europe inset and a legend row on the right.
symbol_map_width <- 12          # in
symbol_map_usable_width <- 11.8 # in, without outer margins
symbol_map_legend_row <- 1.25   # in
symbol_map_text_height <- 0.9   # in, caption and margins
aspect_world <- diff(symbol_world_xlim) / diff(symbol_world_ylim)
aspect_europe <- diff(europe_xlim) / diff(europe_ylim)
right_share <- (symbol_map_usable_width / aspect_world - symbol_map_legend_row) /
  (symbol_map_usable_width / aspect_world + symbol_map_usable_width / aspect_europe)
symbol_map_panel_height <- (1 - right_share) * symbol_map_usable_width / aspect_world
symbol_map_widths <- c(1 - right_share, right_share)
symbol_map_heights <- c(
  right_share * symbol_map_usable_width / aspect_europe,
  symbol_map_legend_row
)
symbol_map_fig_height <- symbol_map_panel_height + symbol_map_text_height
```

```{r country-count-symbol-map}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: !expr symbol_map_fig_height
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-alt: "World map in Equal Earth projection with all countries in light grey and one blue circle per country of work, placed at the centre of the country's mainland, next to an enlarged Europe inset with the same circle scale and count labels. Circle area is proportional to the number of participants."

# Proportional symbols (Wilke ch. 15; audit V13): counts are shown by circle
# area at each country's centre, so large countries do not dominate the way
# they do in a choropleth of raw counts. The circle sits at the area-weighted
# centroid of the country's largest polygon (its mainland), computed in the
# equal-area projection, so e.g. Alaska or overseas territories do not pull it
# away.
polygon_centroid <- function(x, y) {
  x2 <- c(x[-1], x[1])
  y2 <- c(y[-1], y[1])
  cross <- x * y2 - x2 * y
  signed_area <- sum(cross) / 2  # negative for clockwise polygons
  tibble::tibble(
    cx = sum((x + x2) * cross) / (6 * signed_area),
    cy = sum((y + y2) * cross) / (6 * signed_area),
    area = abs(signed_area)
  )
}

country_symbols <- world_map |>
  filter(participants > 0) |>
  group_by(region, group, participants) |>
  reframe(polygon_centroid(x, y)) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  slice_max(area, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Large circles first, so smaller ones are drawn on top and stay visible.
  arrange(desc(participants))

stopifnot(nrow(country_symbols) == nrow(country_counts))

# Round legend values up to the largest count.
symbol_breaks <- c(1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50)
symbol_breaks <- symbol_breaks[symbol_breaks <= max(country_counts$participants)]

# Europe inset: most participants work in Europe, where the circles overlap on
# the world map. The inset shows the same countries enlarged; circle sizes use
# the same scale in both panels (fixed limits), so a circle means the same count
# everywhere. Extents and layout: chunk country-symbol-map-geometry.
symbol_size_scale <- function(show_legend = TRUE) {
  scale_size_area(
    "Participants",
    max_size = 16,
    limits = c(0, max(country_counts$participants)),
    breaks = symbol_breaks,
    guide = if (show_legend) {
      guide_legend(
        nrow = 1,
        title.position = "top",
        title.hjust = 0.5,
        label.position = "bottom",
        override.aes = list(alpha = 0.8)
      )
    } else {
      "none"
    }
  )
}

symbol_map_layers <- list(
  geom_polygon(
    data = world_map,
    aes(x, y, group = group),
    fill = "#E3E3E3",
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.15
  ),
  geom_point(
    data = country_symbols,
    aes(cx, cy, size = participants),
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#3182BD",
    colour = "white",
    alpha = 0.8,
    stroke = 0.6
  )
)

country_symbol_world <- ggplot() +
  symbol_map_layers +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = europe_xlim[1], xmax = europe_xlim[2],
    ymin = europe_ylim[1], ymax = europe_ylim[2],
    fill = NA, colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  symbol_size_scale(show_legend = TRUE) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = symbol_world_xlim, ylim = symbol_world_ylim, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 15)

country_symbol_europe <- ggplot() +
  symbol_map_layers +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(country_symbols, participants >= 5),
    aes(cx, cy, label = participants),
    family = "Lato",
    size = 4,
    colour = "white",
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  # Panel label inside the frame (a plot title would float above the panel,
  # aligned to the taller world map).
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = europe_xlim[1] + 0.02 * diff(europe_xlim),
    y = europe_ylim[2] - 0.03 * diff(europe_ylim),
    label = "Europe",
    hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
    family = "Lato", size = 5, colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  symbol_size_scale(show_legend = FALSE) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = europe_xlim, ylim = europe_ylim, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 15) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.4)
  )

# Right column: the Europe inset with the size legend under it, so the space
# beside the world map is used instead of a separate legend row.
# One flat layout (a nested guide_area() would not receive the legend):
# A = world map over both rows, B = Europe inset, C = legend under the inset.
# Widths, heights and the figure height come from country-symbol-map-geometry.
country_symbol_map <- country_symbol_world + country_symbol_europe +
  patchwork::guide_area() +
  patchwork::plot_layout(
    design = "AB\nAC",
    widths = symbol_map_widths,
    heights = symbol_map_heights,
    guides = "collect"
  ) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    caption = paste0(
      "N = ", sum(country_counts$participants),
      " respondents with a country of work; ",
      n_distinct(country_counts$map_region), " countries.",
      " Circle area is proportional to the number of participants, on the same",
      " scale in both panels; numbers in the inset are counts of 5 or more.",
      " Equal Earth projection."
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(
        hjust = 0, size = 11, colour = "grey30", family = "Lato"
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4)
    )
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, family = "Lato"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13, family = "Lato")
  )

country_symbol_map

ggsave_st(
  project_path("figures", "country_work_participant_symbol_map.png"),
  country_symbol_map,
  width = symbol_map_width,
  height = symbol_map_fig_height,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 180,
  device = ragg::agg_png,

)
```

```{r software-reduced-data}
#| cache: false
# Same grouping as the reduced combined figure below: tools chosen by fewer
# than 4% of respondents, and "Other", are pooled; a respondent who chose
# several of them is counted once.
software_reduced_other_items <- software %>%
  filter(Freq > 0, percent_score < 4 | software == "Other") %>%
  pull(item)

software_reduced <- software %>%
  filter(Freq > 0, percent_score >= 4, software != "Other") %>%
  bind_rows(
    data %>%
      select(ID, all_of(software_reduced_other_items)) %>%
      pivot_longer(-ID, names_to = "item", values_to = "response") %>%
      group_by(ID) %>%
      summarise(selected = any(response == "Checked", na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      summarise(Freq = sum(selected)) %>%
      mutate(
        item = NA_character_,
        software = "Other (each <4%)",
        percent_score = Freq / n_total * 100
      )
  ) %>%
  # Other last, the rest by share
  mutate(order = if_else(software == "Other (each <4%)", -Inf, percent_score))

software_reduced_plot <- function(plot_data, label_column = "software") {
  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(percent_score, forcats::fct_reorder(.data[[label_column]], order))
  ) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, fill = "#6BAED6") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percent_score), "%")),
              hjust = -0.15, size = 8) +  # ~23 pt, matches the 20 pt axis text in the larger figure
    scale_x_continuous(
      "Percent of respondents",
      labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * n_total / 100, name = "Number of respondents"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.10))
    ) +
    labs(y = NULL) +  # section heading is the title (Wilke ch. 22)
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    plot_theme(base_size = 20) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 22),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
    )
}
```

### Grouped with logos

```{r software-reduced-logos}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: '\* Survey answer "My own code in …" for the language shown.'
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
# Experiment: tool branding in the axis labels. Where a tool has its own
# lettering, only the lettering is used (no icon); otherwise logo + name. Tools
# without a usable logo stay text. Logo sources: figures/software_logos/SOURCES.md
# gridtext places images on the text baseline and cannot lower them, so text
# next to a logo is raised instead: <sup> lifts it by half the font ascent and
# the style attribute restores the full 20 pt size. Logos beside text use
# logo_text_height so their middle lines up with the raised text.
logo_text_height <- 32
logo <- function(file, height = logo_text_height) {
  sprintf(
    "<img src='%s' height='%d'/>",
    project_path("figures", "software_logos", file),
    height
  )
}
# One <sup> lifts about 7 pt; two nested lifts bring the text to the logo middle.
# Branded lettering with descenders (python): one lift aligns the baselines.
lift <- function(text) sprintf("<sup style='font-size:20pt'>%s</sup>", text)
mid <- function(text) {
  sprintf("<sup style='font-size:20pt'><sup style='font-size:20pt'>%s</sup></sup>", text)
}

# Equal letter size across all lettering: cap height (all-caps words) or
# ascender height (mixed words), measured per image so each is ~15 pt. "*" = "My own code in ...", explained in the caption.
star <- "<sup style='font-size:24pt'>*</sup>"  # 'My own code in', see caption
software_logo_labels <- c(
  "EEGLAB" = logo("eeglab_text.png", 21),
  "MNE-Python" = logo("mne.png", 16),
  "FieldTrip" = logo("fieldtrip_text.png", 20),
  "ERPLAB" = logo("erplab_text.png", 21),
  "ggplot" = logo("ggplot2_text.png", 21),
  "SPM" = logo("spm_text.png", 16),
  "Brain Vision Analyser" = logo("brainvision_analyzer_text.png", 32),
  "Brainstorm" = logo("brainstorm_text.png", 18),
  "LIMO" = logo("limo_text.png", 17),
  "My own code in MATLAB" = paste0(star, logo("matlab_text.png", 17)),
  "My own code in Python" = paste0(star, logo("python_text.png", 21)),
  "My own code in R" = paste0(star, logo("r.png", 18)),
  "Other (each <4%)" = "*Other*<br>(each &lt;4%)"
)

software_reduced %>%
  mutate(
    label = coalesce(unname(software_logo_labels[software]), software)
  ) %>%
  software_reduced_plot("label") +
  theme(axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 20, lineheight = 0.7))
```

## Combined figures

```{r participant-characteristics-figure}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 10

make_characteristic_plot <- function(
  plot_data,
  label_column,
  title,
  bar_width = 0.7,
  label_size = 20,
  print = FALSE,
  x_max = 100  # axis end in %; below 100 for panels whose bars stay short
) {
  # Site sizes (nominal, drawn at 96/180 of nominal by showtext), or print sizes
  # in true pt (audit V7); value-label size in mm as ggplot2 expects.
  s <- if (print) {
    list(base = print_text$text, title = print_text$text, axis = print_text$small,
         labels = print_text$text, value = print_text$small / ggplot2::.pt,
         margin = margin(3, 10, 3, 3))
  } else {
    list(base = 20, title = 26, axis = 20, labels = label_size, value = 8,
         margin = margin(8, 20, 8, 8))
  }
  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[label_column]])) %>%
    mutate(
      display_label = forcats::fct_reorder(
        factor(.data[[label_column]]),
        other_last(.data[[label_column]], percent_score)
      )
    )

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = percent_score, y = display_label)) +
    geom_col(width = bar_width, fill = "#6BAED6") +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = percent_label(percent_score)),
      hjust = -0.15,
      size = s$value
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0, x_max),
      breaks = seq(0, x_max, if (x_max <= 50) 10 else 25),
      labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = format_category_labels) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Percent of respondents", y = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    plot_theme(base_size = s$base) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = s$title),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = s$axis),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = s$axis),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = s$labels),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = s$margin
    )
}

experience_combined <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(A001), A001 != "") %>%
  count(level = A001, name = "Freq") %>%
  mutate(percent_score = Freq / sum(Freq) * 100)

    country_work = as.character(country_work),
    Freq,
    percent_score
  )

field_combined <- field %>%

software_combined <- software %>%
  filter(Freq > 0, !is.na(software), software != "")

p_experience <- make_characteristic_plot(
  experience_combined,
  "level",
  "Self-assessed level"
)
p_country <- make_characteristic_plot(
  country_combined,
  "country_work",

)
p_field <- make_characteristic_plot(

)

)

participant_characteristics_figure <-
  (p_experience + p_field) /

  plot_layout(heights = c(0.65, 1.35)) +

    tag_levels = "A",
    caption = paste0(
      "Bars show percentages of respondents with valid responses. ",
      "Multiple software selections were permitted."
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
      plot.caption = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "italic",
        family = "Lato",
        size = 18
      )
```

Countries below 2% and software below 4% are grouped into Other. Flags identify
countries, and lettering or logos identify software. The last tab shows the

```{r participant-characteristics-icon-labels}
#| include: false
# Label helpers shared by the three tabs below. icons = FALSE gives plain text:
# country names, and "MATLAB (own code)" for the "My own code in ..." answers.
country_icon_labels <- function(labels) {
  labels <- as.character(labels)
  is_other <- startsWith(labels, "Other")
  country_names <- sub("\\n.*$", "", labels)
  formatted <- flag_label(country_names, height = 15, width = 24)
  formatted[is_other] <- "*Other*<br>(each &lt;2%)"
  formatted
}

software_icon_labels <- function(labels) {
  labels <- as.character(labels)
  is_other <- startsWith(labels, "Other")
  software_names <- sub("\\n.*$", "", labels)
  formatted <- coalesce(
    unname(software_logo_labels[software_names]),
    software_names
  )
  formatted[is_other] <- "*Other*<br>(each &lt;4%)"
  formatted
}

plain_country_labels <- function(labels) {
  labels |>
    as.character() |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("<", "&lt;") |>
    stringr::str_replace("^Other\\n", "*Other*<br>")
}

plain_software_labels <- function(labels) {
  labels |>
    as.character() |>
    stringr::str_replace("^My own code in (.*)$", "\\1 (own code)") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("<", "&lt;") |>
    stringr::str_replace("^Other\\n", "*Other*<br>")
}
```

#### Compact

```{r participant-characteristics-icons-compact}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 9.2
#| fig-cap: 'Level and research field are parts of a whole, so each is shown as one stacked bar (A); this leaves more height for country and software (B, C). B and C have their own axis ranges (0–40% and 0–75%). Flags indicate country of work, not nationality. Multiple software selections were permitted in C. An asterisk denotes the survey answer "My own code in …".'

# Parts of a whole as one 100% bar each (Wilke ch. 10); segments ordered as
# the answer scale (level) or by share (field), labelled directly so no legend
# is needed. Segments too narrow for an inside label are labelled to the right.
composition <- bind_rows(
  experience_combined %>%
    transmute(
      question = "Self-assessed level",
      category = level,
      percent_score,
      order = match(level, c("Beginner", "Intermediate", "Expert"))
    ),
  field_combined %>%
    transmute(
      question = "Research field",
      category = field,
      percent_score,
      order = rank(-percent_score, ties.method = "first")
    )
) %>%
  group_by(question) %>%
  arrange(order, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    xmax = cumsum(percent_score),
    xmin = xmax - percent_score,
    shade = order / max(order),
    inside = percent_score >= 15,
    label = paste0(category, " ", round(percent_score), "%")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # Colour (audit V15): the ordered level gets a light-to-dark ramp; research
    # field is nominal, so all its segments share one mid-blue (the bar colour
    # of panels B and C), separated by the white gaps and named by their labels.
    fill_colour = if_else(
      question == "Research field",
      "#6BAED6",
      scales::seq_gradient_pal("#C6DBEF", "#2171B5")(scales::rescale(shade))
    ),
    question = factor(question, c("Research field", "Self-assessed level"))
  )

composition_y <- as.numeric(composition$question)

# Print copies of the icon labels (audit V7): showtext draws site text at 96/180
# of its nominal size but print text at true size, while images keep their size
# on both. So font sizes in the markup scale by text_k and image sizes by img_k.
scale_markup <- function(labels, text_k, img_k) {
  scale_number <- function(x, pattern, k, digits) {
    stringr::str_replace_all(x, pattern, \(m) stringr::str_replace(
      m, "[0-9.]+",
      as.character(round(as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(m, "[0-9.]+")) * k, digits))
    ))
  }
  labels %>%
    scale_number("font-size:[0-9.]+pt", text_k, 1) %>%
    scale_number("(width|height)='[0-9.]+'", img_k, 0)
}

# Site version, or with print = TRUE the print version (full journal width,
# 8 pt text, 7 pt ticks and value labels).
# Axis ends: each bar panel gets its own range (no country above 24%, no tool
# above 63%); the panels answer different questions (country sums to 100%,
# software allows several answers), so a shared 0-100% axis only wasted space.
make_participant_characteristics_icons_compact <- function(print = FALSE, icons = TRUE,
                                                         country_max = 40,
                                                         software_max = 75) {
  # Site sizes are nominal (drawn at 96/180 by showtext); print sizes are true pt.
  s <- if (print) {
    list(base = print_text$text, question = print_text$text, ticks = print_text$small,
         segment = print_text$small / ggplot2::.pt, margin = margin(3, 42, 3, 3),
         rect_line = 0.4, tag = print_text$text,
         country = print_text$text, software = print_text$text, lineheight = 0.9)
  } else {
    list(base = 20, question = 22, ticks = 20, segment = 7,
         margin = margin(8, 150, 8, 8), rect_line = 1, tag = 18,
         country = 22, software = 20, lineheight = 0.75)
  }
  # Image sizes follow the text (print text / site text as drawn, 96/180), less
  # 20%: print rows are closer together relative to the text than site rows.
  img_shrink <- 0.8
  country_labels <- \(labels) {
    if (!icons) return(plain_country_labels(labels))
    out <- country_icon_labels(labels)
    if (!print) return(out)
    scale_markup(out, s$country / 22, img_shrink * s$country / (22 * 96 / 180))
  }
  software_labels <- \(labels) {
    if (!icons) return(plain_software_labels(labels))
    out <- software_icon_labels(labels)
    if (!print) return(out)
    scale_markup(out, s$software / 20, img_shrink * s$software / (20 * 96 / 180))
  }

  p_composition <- ggplot(composition) +
    geom_rect(
      aes(
        xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,
        ymin = composition_y - 0.36, ymax = composition_y + 0.36,
        fill = fill_colour
      ),
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = s$rect_line
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = \(d) filter(d, inside),
      aes(
        x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
        y = as.numeric(question),
        label = label,
        colour = shade > 0.8
      ),
      family = "Lato",
      size = s$segment,
      lineheight = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = \(d) filter(d, !inside),
      aes(x = 100, y = as.numeric(question), label = label),
      hjust = -0.08,
      family = "Lato",
      size = s$segment
    ) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 100),
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
      labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq_along(levels(composition$question)),
      labels = levels(composition$question),
      expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Percent of respondents", y = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    plot_theme(base_size = s$base) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = s$question, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = s$ticks),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = s$margin
    )

  axis_end_mark <- x_axis_end_mark(s$base, size = if (print) 0.55 else 1)

  p_country <- make_characteristic_plot(
    country_over_3, "country_work", "Country of work", print = print,
    x_max = country_max
  ) +
    axis_end_mark +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = country_labels) +
    theme(axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(
      size = s$country, lineheight = s$lineheight
    ))

  p_software <- make_characteristic_plot(
    software_over_3, "software", "Software used", print = print,
    x_max = software_max
  ) +
    axis_end_mark +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = software_labels) +
    theme(axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(
      size = s$software, lineheight = if (print) s$lineheight else 0.7
    ))

  p_composition /
    (p_country + p_software) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(0.42, 1.58)) +
    plot_annotation(
      tag_levels = "A",
      theme = theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = s$tag))
    )
}

participant_characteristics_icons_compact <-
  make_participant_characteristics_icons_compact()

participant_characteristics_icons_compact

    units = "in",

    bg = "white"
  )

  # Print version: full journal width.
  ggsave_print(
    project_path("figures", "participant_characteristics_icons_compact.pdf"),
    make_participant_characteristics_icons_compact(print = TRUE),
    width = print_width[["full"]],
    height = 5.6
  )
}
```

## Summary of the sample results

```{r sample-summary-text}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
# Every number below comes from objects computed above. Shares are of the
# respondents who answered the question; "Other" is not named as a category.
sample_share <- function(n, total) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * n / total)
sample_top <- function(df, label, n = 3) {
  rows <- df |>
    filter(.data[[label]] != "Other", Freq > 0) |>
    arrange(desc(Freq)) |>
    slice_head(n = n)
  knitr::combine_words(sprintf(
    "%s (%.0f%%)", as.character(rows[[label]]), rows$percent_score
  ))
}

sample_experience <- data |>
  filter(!is.na(A001)) |>
  count(A001, name = "Freq") |>
  mutate(A001 = factor(A001, levels = c("Beginner", "Intermediate", "Expert"))) |>
  arrange(A001)
sample_n_countries <- n_distinct(country_responses$country_work)
sample_country_counts <- country_responses |>
  count(country_work, name = "Freq") |>
  mutate(
    country_work = if_else(country_work == "United Kingdom", "UK", country_work),
    percent_score = Freq / sum(Freq) * 100
  )
sample_largest_continent <- continent |> slice_max(Freq, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

- **Included sample.** `r nrow(data)` respondents who started after the launch date and
  completed the questionnaire. The median completion time was
  `r sprintf("%.1f", median(as.numeric(data$TIME_SUM), na.rm = TRUE) / 60)` minutes.
  `r length(flagged_ids)` participants are flagged for possibly careless answering and
  kept in all main analyses.
- **Self-assessed experience.**
  `r knitr::combine_words(sprintf("%s %s", sample_experience$A001, sample_share(sample_experience$Freq, sum(sample_experience$Freq))))`
  (n = `r sum(sample_experience$Freq)`).
- **Country of work.** `r nrow(country_responses)` respondents named
  `r sample_n_countries` countries; the most frequent were
  `r sample_top(sample_country_counts, "country_work")`.
  `r sprintf("%.0f%%", sample_largest_continent$percent_score)` worked in
  `r sample_largest_continent$continent`.
- **Research field.** The largest groups were `r sample_top(field, "field", n = 2)`.
- **Software** (multiple selections). The most frequently used tools were
  `r sample_top(software, "software")`.
